div.head: First: of the Mother of God.
div.ab: Hail to thee from all! O holy one, Mary, Mother of God: excellent and precious Treasure of all the habitable world: Lamp brightly shining: Mansion of the Incomprehensible: pure Sanctuary of the Creator of all creatures. Hail to thee! by whom He was tended that taketh away the sin of the world and redeemeth it.

div.head: Another.
div.ab: In the mountains of Horeb he saw thee—even Moses the marvellous Prophet—O Virgin holy, as a fire set in the Bush, and blazing therein: and the Bush was not consumed. Thee, again, the Ladder portrayed, which Jacob the Just saw in the wilderness, whereby the Watchers [angels] did ascend to Heaven and descend. Likewise did the son of Jesse take his spiritual harp and begin to say upon it: As gentle rain that cometh down upon the earth, so did God come down and abide in a Virgin. Wherefore let the maidens and virgins of the Hebrews come, with their timbrels in their hands, and play in the Holy Spirit before the King's Son, and say: Blessed art thou, Mary, for What thou hast brought forth.

div.head: First: of the Mother of God.
div.ab: How shall we praise thee, O thou pure one? Alone thou art holy in all things; for to all the faithful together thou pourest out helps and strength. For all we that are in the world are looking and waiting for the hope that cometh from thee, O pure one. Make firm the faith of us all; and to all the world give peace. Wherefore we the faithful do praise thee, as that Throne of the Cherubim and that Bridechamber of Eden. Do thou entreat for us all, and make supplication, that the souls of us all be delivered from wrath.

div.head: Of the Mother of God.
div.ab: Who sufficeth to praise thy festival, Virgin pure and holy? And who is able to speak of thy conceiving and Childbearing, which was marvellous, O Virgin pure and holy? For the Living Fire dwelt in a womb of flesh, and it thereby was not consumed! Entreat for us all by thy prayers and petitions, that the souls of us all be delivered from wrath.

div.head: Of the Mother of God.
div.ab: Whereas Moses the son of Amram depicted thee in the Bush unburnt, thou hast brought forth a Hart, yea a Gazelle. And the Hart is Christ; for (so) did Solomon call Him. Now the Bush was ablaze with the Fire; but the leaves therof were comely and fair, and they were not scorched. And as for thee, O Virgin, thy womb was not hurt by that consuming Fire. And from the Sling of David went forth the Stone which slew Goliath. Thee it portrayed, what time thou barest the Branch (Ṣemḥa) that slew Death, and crushed the serpent with His Cross, and the adder was destroyed and vanquished. And with joy we cry out: Heaven and earth bless ye the Lord, with the Virgin pure and holy for evermore.

div.head: Of the Mother of God (from the) Greek.
div.ab: Exalted art thou above (all) minds, and high above the world, and more glorious than the ranks of the many-eyed Cherubim, bright Mother of God. For in splendour thou hast authority over all that is in creation: insomuch that thou hast borne the Creator in thy womb. Wherefore all we do magnify thee, O Mother of God.

div.head: Another (from the) Greek.
div.ab: By the name of spiritual Mountain Daniel called thee; but Isaiah (called thee) the Virgin that bare Emmanuel. And Gideon, the famous Judge, saw thee as a Fleece. But David called thee the Ark, and Ezekiel the Door. Gabriel the Archangel cried out: Hail to thee, full of grace! The Lord is with thee, O blessed one.

div.head: Another (from the) Greek.
div.ab: O Virgin pure, saith the Angel of fire, receive the words of him that bringeth thee tidings. Gaze steadfastly and see the purpose of the Most High. Thy body and thy soul prepare for Him that fashioned thee; for it hath pleased Him, the Immortal, thence to become incarnate, and to shine forth upon creation. And I with joy will cry out: Bless ye, all ye works and creatures of the Lord, the Lord of creation, and extol and praise and bless Him for ever.

div.head: First: of the Mother of God.
div.ab: Pure Mother, as thou art wont to help our poverty—for thou seest us earthly ones, that our end is come and, lo, we are perishing—have pity upon us by thy prayers. Virgin pure and holy, do thou make supplication for us continually, that we may not perish by reason of our wickedness. Entreat and ask, O blessed one, the Only-begotten who shined forth from thee, that He would deal mercifully with us through thy prayers, O holy one.

div.head: Of the same.
div.ab: Come in peace, O Ship, laden with new life for men! Come in peace, bright Palace, wherein the King of Kings came down and dwelt! Come in peace, chaste Virgin, Mother of God! Peace be with thee, O thou Blessed! Peace be with thee, O thou Happy! Present for us all a petition to the Only-begotten who shined forth from thee, that He would deal mercifully with us through thy prayers, O holy one.

div.head: Of the Mother of God.
div.ab: O (Virgin) holy, entreat the Only-begotten for sinners; for behold they take refuge in thee. For the rods wherewith they have been beaten from generation to generation, lo, have now set towards (them) and come; and lo, the Destroyer has bent his bow and is fixing his arrow upon the string, that he may shoot as at a (hostile) array. Behold in the heavens, too, and the earth are divers signs of every sort, and plagues that terrify the heart. Wherefore in thee we take refuge. To thy Son we will cry and say: O Chastener of the sinful-hearted, Christ, who smitest and also healest, chasten us in mercy, and win us back in loving-kindness; and spare and have compassion upon us.

div.head: Of the Mother of God.
div.ab: Mary is the Bow of the morning, wherein are stored the treasures of Heaven. And from her God shined forth upon us; and of her the Prophets foretold. David named her the thirsty and weary Land. Daniel (spoke of) the Ancient of days, older than all. Ezekiel (called her) the closed door, whereby God entereth in. Isaiah proclaimed and said: Lo, a Virgin shall conceive and bring forth Emmanuel, who for us became flesh,—even Christ, who came at the end of the times and fulfilled all prophecies. Blessed is He that sent Him!

noteGrp.note: p. 146, n. † The text has named, which gives no sense. I correct by altering the last letter from h to sh.
p. 147, n. ** The author seems to be thinking of the thorn bush of Gen. xxii. 13 as well as of the bush seen by Moses.
p. 147, n. ‡‡ Cf. Jer. xxiii. 5; xxxiii. 15 (Syr.).
p. 148, n. ‡ Or, rational; i.e. as opposed to material or literal.
p. 149, n. * A form of salutation equivalent to Welcome!
p. 149, n. †† The words are masculine and refer to our Lord, though somewhat awkwardly.
